title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: Regular price $11.33; target $12.03 (+6.2%). Past 20% off promotion (2025-06-09) yielded only x0.87 lift, suggesting price sensitivity. No prior 6.2% increase observed, so conservative downward adjustment.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 19.2. The target week has a 6.2% price increase to $12.03, which is above the regular $11.33. Past promotions show average noise-adjusted lift of x1.38, but none at this price point. The recent spike on 2026-09-21 (32 units, x1.67 vs baseline) was not promotion-driven and likely due to seasonal flu onset. With no event, promotion, or price discount, and the classical model suggesting no uplift, the price increase likely suppresses demand. Historical price sensitivity is not directly observed, but the 2025-06-09 20% off saw only x0.87 lift, suggesting price sensitivity. A 6.2% increase likely reduces sales. Adjust down to x0.90 with medium confidence.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 19.2 | 5%-95%: 7.5 - 35.1 | 10%-90%: 9.1 - 31.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-48% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
